newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Milling wheat futures down, maize up in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Milling wheat futures down, maize up in Hungary.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices plummeted on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Tuesday on good crop expectations, traders said.
"Monday's snowfalls removed the threat of an early drought," said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex.
He added that a downward trend on the international markets increased the pressure on domestic prices.
May milling wheat prices went down by the daily allowed 400 forint limit to end at 24,000 forints per tonne. August, October and December also went limit-down.
July milling wheat was the only one that bucked the downward trend rising 200 forints to end at 21,000.
Maize prices rose on large buys but Monostori that the maize futures market remained rumour-driven, with the size of the planted area still being uncertain.
"Nobody knows exactly what the planted area will be," he said. "Estimates run from 700,000 to 1.2 million hectares".
Maize futures rose for May, July, October and December by between 50 and 400 forints, with prices ranging from 17,720 forints for May to 18,610 for December.
Monostori added that prices of the old (1996) crop maize will continue to fluctuate according to how many market players decide to close their positions.
